business-e2e-context · map

Business E2E map

The user journeys through the product, first, and the feature catalog they cross.

Overview

Bunkai (target repo upex-bunkai-tms) is a multi-tenant test management system. Every user acts inside exactly one workspace at a time; the workspace role decides everything they can see and do. The product spine is structural traceability: User Story → Acceptance Criteria → ATC → Test chain → Run → Bug, with coverage and metrics computed from Run verdicts.

Roles the code recognizes

Four workspace roles exist as a DB CHECK on workspace_members.role (supabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql). Only memberships with status = 'active' pass RLS. One additional non-role actor: any authenticated member may hold a Personal Access Token (PAT) and drive the REST API as an agent/CI executor (runs.executor_mode = human | agent | ci).

Role hierarchy and permission matrix

Hierarchy: viewer < member < admin < owner. Ownership is transferred, never invited; invites carry only viewer | member | admin (app/api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/route.ts, lib/workspaces/invites.ts). Role-hierarchy rule BK-60: a role can only issue invites at or below its own level (lib/workspaces/invites.ts:25).

Permission viewer member admin owner
Read projects, ATCs, tests, runs, bugs, dashboards yes yes yes yes
Create/edit ATCs, tests, runs, bugs no yes yes yes
Create/edit modules, stories, ACs, plans, milestones no yes yes yes
Invite members (roles below own), manage invites no no yes yes
Billing overview, Stripe checkout no no no yes
Workspace soft-delete / restore no no no yes

Evidence for row-level owner gating: bunkai_is_workspace_owner (supabase/migrations/0005_rls_helpers.sql), billing routes (owner-only RLS SELECT), workspaces/[id]/route.ts DELETE. Member-level write enforcement is RLS + route guards throughout app/api/v1/. Per-row evidence lives in each persona-* section.

Top journeys (one paragraph each)

  • First ATC (see journey-first-atc): a new member signs in, lands in onboarding, creates a project and module tree, imports or writes a User Story with ACs, and authors the first anchored ATC — the activation loop the product's MVP metrics depend on.
  • Manual run + bug (see journey-manual-run-bug)): a member chains ATCs into a Test, starts a Run, marks step verdicts in the realtime runner, files a native Bug from a failed step with frozen provenance, and finishes or aborts the Run — the core QA working loop.
  • Agent run via API (see journey-api-agent-run)): a human issues a PAT in settings; an AI/CI actor then reads the Test contract, starts an idempotent Run, posts step results and finishes — the same data shapes as the manual loop (executor_mode is the only difference).

Journeys cross-feature-traceability, read paths of journey-manual-run-bug

Journey: first ATC (sign-in to anchored ATC)

Persona: member (PRD: Elena). Entry: public /login. Outcome: first ATC anchored to a US+AC.

  1. Sign in at (auth)/login/page.tsx — password (POST /v1/auth/signin), magic link (POST /v1/auth/magic-link), or OAuth GitHub/Google (app/auth/oauth/[provider]/route.ts, callback app/auth/callback/route.ts).
  2. Middleware redirects authenticated users into the app; new users land in (app)/onboarding/page.tsx (first-workspace bootstrap, POST /v1/me/active-workspace).
  3. Create a project at (app)/projects/new/page.tsx → POST /v1/workspaces/[id]/projects (plan-capped by DB trigger, SQLSTATE 45700).
  4. Build the module tree (project sidebar, POST /v1/projects/[id]/modules, PATCH/DELETE /v1/modules/[id]) — max depth 6 (CHECK on materialized path).
  5. Create a User Story under a module (POST /v1/modules/[id]/user-stories) with Acceptance Criteria (POST /v1/user-stories/[id]/acceptance-criteria); story must reach ready_to_test (requires ≥1 active AC) before test content can anchor.
  6. Author the first ATC at (app)/.../atcs/new/page.tsx → POST /v1/atcs: steps, assertions, classification; acceptance_criterion_ids is .min(1) (lib/atcs/validation.ts:72) — an unanchored ATC is rejected.

Branches and failure points

  • Invalid credentials → sign-in failure path (KATA PROJ-102).
  • Magic-link/OAuth depend on external email/OAuth provider — external-dependency steps, not session-automatable.
  • Plan limit reached → project create fails with SQLSTATE 45700.
  • Module depth > 6 → module create rejected (409/ CHECK).
  • Story still draft → anchor attempts blocked by the 0017 gate.
  • ATC save without ≥1 AC id → validation error (Zod .min(1)).
  • Concurrent ATC edit → optimistic-lock version conflict.

Data hand-off points: workspace bootstrap (step 2), project insert (step 3), module rows (step 4), story/AC rows (step 5), ATC + join rows (step 6). Entities and state machines: business-data-context sections term-project, term-module, term-user-story, term-atc (that map was a placeholder at generation time — see discovery-gaps).

PRD drift: legacy Journey 1 step "Import User Story from Jira" is not required for this journey — Jira import is a separate Beta feature (feature-jira-import), not a setup step.

Journey: manual run and bug filing

Persona: member (PRD: Elena, day 3). Entry: project tests list. Outcome: a finished Run and, on failure, a native Bug with frozen provenance.

  1. Find or open a Test at (app)/.../tests/[testId]/page.tsx (chains of ATCs; GET /v1/tests/[id], search GET /v1/tests/search).
  2. Start a Run → POST /v1/runs (insert already running; 24h (test_id, start_token) idempotency); snapshot rows run_atcs/run_steps freeze content.
  3. Execute in the runner (app)/.../runs/[runId]/page.tsx; mark each step POST /v1/runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark → parent run_atcs.verdict recomputes (failed > blocked > pending > passed).
  4. On a failed step, file a Bug via the report composer → POST /v1/bugs with provenance (run_id, run_step_id, atc_id frozen; only entry status open).
  5. Finish POST /v1/runs/[id]/finish {passed|failed} or abort POST /v1/runs/[id]/abort {reason}; leftover pending steps force-skipped on finish.
  6. Observers see updates: Supabase Realtime on run_atcs/run_steps (see discovery-gaps for the realtime conflict), activity feed and notifications fan out from activity_log triggers.

Branches and failure points

  • Browser refresh mid-run — state must resume from the last marked step (PRD expectation; verify).
  • Two members start the same Test — two separate Run rows (distinct start_tokens).
  • Idle run > 4 min — pg_cron sweep closes it as aborted (supabase/migrations/0075_run_inactivity_sweep.sql).
  • Abort is idempotent; finish accepts only terminal verdicts.
  • Bug create without module/provenance consistency → RPC/trigger rejection (bunkai_create_bug).
  • Bug status is forward-only (open → in_progress → resolved → closed); reopening is DB-blocked — regression = new bug.

Money/data hand-off: the Run snapshot at step 2 is the point where history freezes; bug provenance freezes at step 4. Pointers: business-data-context term-run, term-bug; business-api-context run/bug endpoint groups (see discovery-gaps for map status).

Journey: agent-driven run via API

Persona: any member acting as an API consumer (PRD persona "Karim", the AI Test Agent). Entry: PAT issued in the browser. Outcome: a Run executed entirely over REST with the same data shapes as the manual loop.

  1. Precondition (human, browser): a member issues a PAT at (app)/settings/tokens/page.tsx → POST /v1/tokens — issuance is browser-session only; PAT auth structurally cannot mint new PATs (cookie-only posture, tokens/cookie-only-posture.test.ts). Raw secret shown once.
  2. Agent authenticates: GET /v1/me with Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_…; principal resolution mints a user JWT so RLS applies identically to the cookie rail (lib/api/principal.ts).
  3. Read the Test contract: GET /v1/tests/[id] (chains + ATC content).
  4. Start the Run: POST /v1/runs with start_token — same token within 24h returns the same Run (idempotent replay).
  5. Report step results: POST /v1/runs/[id]/steps/[stepId]/mark per step (shipped endpoint — see PRD drift below).
  6. Optionally file a Bug on failure: POST /v1/bugs.
  7. Finish: POST /v1/runs/[id]/finish with passed|failed.

Branches and failure points

  • Expired/revoked PAT → 401; PAT revoked automatically on workspace deletion / member exit.
  • Some routes are cookie-only by gateway posture — the agent receives a structural rejection, not a role error.
  • Idempotency collision (same start_token) returns the existing Run — must not double-apply.
  • RLS scoping identical to UI: a token can never cross workspaces.

PRD drift (verified): legacy Journey 3 cites POST /runs/{id}/steps/{step_id}/result and a generic finish — the shipped endpoints are .../mark and finish-with-verdict; legacy also cites POST /api/v1/runs rate limits (100 write/600 read) and an idempotency header on every POST — rate limiting is not implemented (infra map nfr-security NFR-SEC-007) and run idempotency is the start_token mechanism, not a generic header.

Cross-feature flow: structural traceability

The product thesis spans authoring, execution and reporting: User Story → AC → ATC (M:N via atc_acceptance_criteria, mandatory user_story_id FK on atcs) → Test chain (test_steps) → Run snapshots (run_atcs/run_steps) → latest verdict → coverage (GET /v1/projects/[id]/coverage) and the chain view (GET /v1/projects/[id]/traceability, UI (app)/.../traceability/page.tsx).

  • Handoffs: anchoring enforced at authoring (validation + schema); verdicts computed only in execution; coverage reads only run_atcs (never the dead atcs.status column, migration 0050).
  • Failure modes: archived module subtree (US/AC/ATC soft-deleted, tests/bugs not cascaded) leaves chains pointing at archived content; export snapshot RPC must stay consistent.
  • Roles: members write the chain; viewers consume the read views.

Cross-feature flow: bug feedback loop

A failed run step becomes a Bug (frozen provenance), the Bug moves through a forward-only status machine with assignment, and quality signals fan out: notifications/activity from triggers, defect heatmap (GET /v1/projects/[id]/bugs/heatmap), recovery-cycle metric (GET /v1/projects/[id]/metrics/recovery-cycles), optional daily email digest (Resend, cron POST /v1/admin/send-digest).

  • Handoffs: run step → bug create; bug status → notify reporter+assignee (minus actor); bugs → metrics/heatmap reads.
  • Failure modes: digest idempotency (one row per user per day, 0078); notification preference gates (mentions locked on); reopen is DB-blocked so regressions must be filed as new bugs.

Discovery gaps

What could not be verified, was found aspirational, or needs a team decision (checked 2026-10-10).

  • Overview journey figures deferred: diagram-design style gate not resolved (no .diagram-design marker). Figures can be added per-section later; every fact is in the text.
  • business-data-context and business-api-context maps were placeholders when this map was generated — journey/feature pointers to their section ids are forward references (may already be generated by parallel tasks).
  • Realtime conflict: the legacy feature map claims Supabase Realtime works (FEAT-RUN-003, migration + channel test); the infra map could not confirm a live push path in app code. Verify on a deployed environment before citing realtime as shipped.
  • PRD Journey 3 drift: legacy step names (POST /runs/{id}/steps/{step_id}/result, generic finish, per-POST idempotency header, rate limits) do not match the shipped contract (mark endpoint, finish-with-verdict, start_token, no rate limiting). The journey section reflects shipped reality; the PRD needs an update.
  • Per-role test accounts: only a generic QA_E2E_USER_EMAIL/QA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD pair exists in the QA repo's .env.example. No owner/admin/viewer-specific keys were found — needed for RBAC suites.
  • Aspirational / not shipped (excluded from the inventory): member role-change and admin member-removal endpoints; ownership-transfer endpoint; invite email delivery; project update/delete; test-chain content edit/delete; test-plan delete; milestone delete/status/completion; GitHub PR ↔ ATC linking; bidirectional Jira sync; rate limiting and CSP (legacy NFR targets with no code); Sentry/PostHog/Cloudflare R2 (legacy claims with no code, infra map).
  • atcs.status dead column — no production writer since migration 0050. Deprecate or wire a writer? Team decision required.
  • feature_flags table has no runtime reads — dead infra or unfinished flag system?
  • Missing migrations 0079, 0080 in the sequence — reverted, or absent from repo?
  • user_view_state write path only partially verified (legacy data-map note) — which views persist?
  • New projects get no seeded environments (migration 0031 seeds only pre-existing projects) — expected product behavior?
  • No GET /projects list endpoint and no project update/delete route — intentional API surface or WIP? No UI screen exists either.
  • DBHub MCP unavailable during generation — schema claims rest on migrations 0001–0088, not live-DB inspection. Re-verify RLS policies and trigger behavior when DBHUB_* credentials are configured.
  • Journeys were traced from routes and legacy PRD tables, not from recorded real sessions — step-level timing expectations (e.g. "bug filing < 90s", "tree renders < 800ms") are PRD targets, not measurements.
  • Invite hierarchy (BK-60) verified from code comments and validation logic (lib/workspaces/invites.ts:25); full negative-path behavior (what error the caller sees) not executed in this pass.
